mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months above 2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the identified rising rate period, or the effect size is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05 in a regression controlling for FEDFUNDS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in a month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative or show no statistically significant correlation with the labor strength signal (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future earnings and supports higher equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth exceeds 0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day log returns are negative despite the demand acceleration signal, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% followed by a rebound exceeding 1% in the subsequent month suggests a supply-side shock that initially suppresses demand but is quickly offset by market optimism, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -2% in month t, then rises > +1% in month t+1
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain negative during the recovery period, or the signal shows no predictive power (out-of-sample p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 1% for four consecutive months, it indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers real interest rates, encouraging risk-taking in equities and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or the real interest rate proxy (e.g., 10y Treasury yield minus FEDFUNDS) shows no significant correlation with SPX returns (R-squared < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a rise in layoffs (PAYEMS) suggests labor market tightness is deteriorating, raising fears of slower growth and prompting equity sell-offs that drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by at least 15% in a month while PAYEMS increases by at least 10%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive or the interaction signal shows no predictive power (out-of-sample p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two months suggests deflationary pressure, lowering growth expectations and pushing down equity valuations, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for two consecutive months below 2%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the ratio of new home construction (not directly observable in the given catalog, so this will be omitted) — instead, we use a supply proxy: a sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 3% for two months followed by a flat month indicates supply constraints, raising uncertainty and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 3% in two consecutive months and remains flat in the third
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the signal shows no predictive power (out-of-sample p > 0.05).
